section: Presiding officers - Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman; Secretariat; sessions, adjournment, prorogation, dissolution

accepted.s:
Under Article 86 of the Constitution of India, the President may
1. Address either House of Parliament separately or both Houses together.
2. Require the attendance of members for the purpose of the address.
3. Send messages to either House with respect to a pending Bill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Article 86 empowers the President to address either House or both Houses together, require members' attendance and send messages to either House regarding pending Bills.
accepted.tq: Test the exact scope of Article 86 by separating the President’s powers of addressing, requiring attendance and sending messages.

accepted.s:
The special address delivered by the President under Article 87 is made at which of the following occasions?
1. The first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha.
2. The first session of Parliament in each year.
3. Every session immediately after prorogation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Article 87 provides for the President’s special address at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year. It is not required after every prorogation.
accepted.tq: Identify the two constitutionally specified occasions and reject the overbroad time-based statement.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Articles 86 and 87 of the Constitution?
o: Article 86 relates to the address by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, whereas Article 87 relates to the address by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Article 86 concerns the President’s special address at the first session of each year, whereas Article 87 concerns messages to either House.
Article 86 deals exclusively with the address after a general election, whereas Article 87 deals with the annual Budget session.
Article 86 permits the President to address either House or both Houses at any time, whereas Article 87 provides for a special address at specified opening sessions.
accepted.x: Article 86 deals with the President’s general power to address either House or both Houses and send messages. Article 87 prescribes the special address at the first session after a general election and the first session of each year.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely related constitutional provisions by matching each Article with its distinctive feature.

accepted.s: The address of the President outlining the policies of the Government is debated in Parliament through a:
accepted.x: The President’s address outlining Government policy is debated through a Motion of Thanks in Parliament.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional address with the parliamentary motion that follows it.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the secretarial arrangements of Parliament under Article 98:
1. Each House of Parliament has separate secretarial staff.
2. Posts common to both Houses may be created.
3. Parliament may regulate recruitment and conditions of service by law.
4. Until Parliament makes such a law, the President may make rules after consulting the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Article 98 provides for separate secretarial staff for each House, permits common posts, authorises Parliament to regulate recruitment by law and allows the President to make rules after consultation with the Speaker and Chairman until such a law is made.
accepted.tq: Cover the full constitutional arrangement by testing the general rule, exception, legislative power and interim rule-making power together.

accepted.s: With reference to Article 98 of the Constitution, which one of the following is correct?
o: The President appoints all secretarial staff directly and Parliament has no power to regulate recruitment by law.
The Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha must have identical secretarial establishments without any common posts.
Each House has separate secretarial staff, although posts common to both Houses may be created.
The executive government alone regulates recruitment to the secretariats of both Houses in all circumstances.
accepted.x: Article 98 establishes separate secretarial staff for each House while permitting the creation of posts common to both Houses.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional general rule and its permitted exception to eliminate statements using exclusive powers.

accepted.s: Until Parliament makes a law regulating recruitment and conditions of service of the secretarial staff of the Houses, rules may be made by the President after consultation with the:
o: Chief Justice of India and Attorney-General of India
Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha and Secretary-General of the Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister and Union Home Minister
Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: In the absence of a law by Parliament, the President may make rules after consulting the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the constitutional consultees from parliamentary officials and ministers.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Secretary-General of a House of Parliament is correct?
1. Each House has a Secretary-General as its head of secretarial staff.
2. The Secretary-General is appointed by the presiding officer of the concerned House.
3. The office holds rank equal to that of the Cabinet Secretary.
4. The secretariat is independent of the executive.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The secretariat of each House is headed by its Secretary-General, appointed by the concerned presiding officer. The Secretary-General has the rank of Cabinet Secretary, and the parliamentary secretariat is independent of the executive.
accepted.tq: Test office, appointing authority, rank and institutional independence as separate elements of one constitutional arrangement.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The office of Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha has remained vacant throughout the 17th Lok Sabha.
2. The office of Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha has remained vacant through the 18th Lok Sabha.
3. The Deputy Speaker’s post has remained continuously occupied in both these Lok Sabhas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Deputy Speaker’s post remained vacant through both the 17th and 18th Lok Sabhas. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Use a present-affairs comparison across two successive Lok Sabhas and reject the directly reversed statement.

accepted.s: An Opposition motion seeking the removal of Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla was reported in which month and year?
accepted.x: The Opposition’s removal motion against Speaker Om Birla was reported in March 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely spaced current-affairs dates by separating the month-year of the event from the month of another reported development.

accepted.s: During the Monsoon Session of 2026, the Lok Sabha recorded how many oral answers, according to the cited assessment of legislative scrutiny?
accepted.x: Only two oral answers were recorded in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon Session of 2026, a point cited in criticism concerning low scrutiny.
accepted.tq: Test a precise session-wise figure rather than relying on a general impression about parliamentary scrutiny.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Office-holder)
 a. Speaker of the first Andhra Pradesh Assembly
 b. Deputy Speaker of the first Andhra Pradesh Assembly
 c. Chairman of the first Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council

List-II (Person)
 i. Madapati Hanumantha Rao
 ii. Kalluri Subbarao
 iii. Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao

Codes:
 a  b  c
1. iii  ii  i
2. ii   iii i
3. iii  i   ii
4. i    ii  iii
accepted.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the Speaker, Kalluri Subbarao was the Deputy Speaker, and Madapati Hanumantha Rao was the first Council Chairman in the first Andhra Pradesh Assembly of 1956.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure office-holder pair and complete the matching after distinguishing the Assembly offices from the Council office.
